chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not involve yourself in a matter for your brother whose harm upon you is greater than its benefit for him.
Ibn Sinan said: It is like if there is a large debt upon a man and you have wealth, so you pay it off on his behalf; your wealth is spent, yet his debt is not cleared.
ai.seo_question: How do you know when helping someone is actually harmful to you?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises against assisting a brother in matters where the harm to the helper outweighs the benefit to the recipient, emphasizing prudent benevolence over reckless generosity. Ibn Sinan clarifies this with an economic example: paying off someone's large debt may deplete your own wealth without actually resolving their financial burden, illustrating the principle of avoiding self-harm in charity. This hadith is often cited by Shia jurists to support the concept of 'la darar wa la dirar' (no harm and no harming) in social and financial interactions.
